item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00094","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C25","C18","C16"],"selected_candidate_label":"C25","confidence":0.97,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C25 plausibly supplied a material drafting template. Both directives address succession after the Secretary and Under Secretary become unavailable, use the same four triggering conditions, designate subordinate officers according to an order fixed from time to time by the Secretary, and conclude by superseding or revoking an earlier succession directive. C18 and C16 are also strong departmental-succession analogues, but C25 has the closest combination of language, compact structure, and discretionary ordering mechanism.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"In case of the death, resignation, absence, or sickness of the Secretary of the Treasury and the Under Secretary of the Treasury","parent_excerpt":"In the case of the absence, sickness, resignation, or death of both the Secretary of Agriculture and the Under Secretary of Agriculture","explanation":"The same four contingencies activate succession only after both the department head and under secretary are unavailable."},{"child_excerpt":"Assistant Secretaries, in the order fixed from time to time by the Secretary of the Treasury.","parent_excerpt":"the Assistant Secretaries of Agriculture, in the order of precedence as determined from time to time by the Secretary of Agriculture","explanation":"Both delegate the ordering of assistant secretaries to the incumbent Secretary through a periodically adjustable designation."},{"child_excerpt":"[DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] of March 18, 1941 ... is hereby revoked.","parent_excerpt":"This order supersedes [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] of June 12, 1948","explanation":"Both close by replacing a specifically identified earlier departmental succession directive."}]}
